bull.b: The long-term Anthropic lease provides substantial contracted revenue visibility and reduces reliance on near-term bitcoin-mining economics. Its scale also establishes TeraWulf as a meaningful AI infrastructure provider, supporting recurring cash-flow potential as capacity is delivered.

Rapid growth in HPC leasing shows the business is transitioning toward a more diversified, contracted infrastructure model. A larger recurring lease base can improve revenue predictability and reduce exposure to bitcoin prices, network difficulty, and mining reward changes over time.

Expanded power access and stronger project execution frameworks increase the company’s ability to develop large-scale AI data centers. Utility agreements, credit support, and an experienced EPC partner together improve the platform’s capacity to convert demand into operating assets.

bear.b: Severe losses below gross profit show that current revenue and gross margin are not yet sufficient to cover operating and other expenses. Until new HPC capacity contributes at scale, sustained losses may continue to weaken profitability and constrain internally funded growth.

Deeply negative free cash flow combined with elevated leverage creates continuing dependence on financing and project monetizations. Large funding needs can limit strategic flexibility, increase interest burden, and make execution more sensitive to delays or weaker operating results.

Labor shortages and evolving customer requirements could delay commissioning or raise project costs while capacity is still being built. The gap between reported and target leasing margins also indicates that near-term economics remain pressured before contracted capacity fully enters service.
